title: Recover XOR-hidden components and exploit cancellation between them
summary: Useful for discovering latent polynomial/tensor structure and for signed partition functions where zeros in transformed local weights remove most global configurations.
content: The centroid of a cubic third polar form exposes direct summands hidden by invertible binary coordinate changes; recovery is complete for a scrambled direct sum of three-variable cubic products. Transform lower-degree terms too. For supplied blocks f=sum f_i+q, Fourier support of the quadratic coupling gives cost poly(N)*(2^r+sum_i 2^b_i), where r is its polar rank. A different exact leaf handles connected loopless cubic port graphs: one abc phase per vertex and one xy coupling per edge has gap 2^e+(-2)^v(-1)^e, despite full global coupling rank. Twisted variants use 2-by-2 edge transfers and contract forced implications before enumeration.
whenToUse: Useful for discovering latent polynomial/tensor structure and for signed partition functions where zeros in transformed local weights remove most global configurations.
limitations: The centroid promise matters; large centroid dimension alone does not guarantee recovery. Lower-degree couplings cannot be discarded. General twists can leave exponential residual enumeration. These are complementary structural leaves, not a general cubic solver.
